history.heading: Portuguese trading post
paragraphs: Macau, on the southern coast of China across the Pearl River estuary from Hong Kong, was a fishing area when Portuguese traders settled there in the 1550s with permission from Ming officials. It became Europe's first and longest-lasting colony in East Asia and a key hub for trade between China, Japan and Europe, and for Catholic missions in Asia.
Portugal declared full sovereignty in the mid-19th century. Macau declined as a port after Hong Kong's rise but became known for gambling.

history.heading: Return to China
paragraphs: Following a 1987 agreement between Portugal and China, Macau was handed over to China on 20 December 1999, becoming a Special Administrative Region under the "one country, two systems" principle until at least 2049. Opening the casino market to foreign operators in 2002 led to rapid growth.

culture.heading: East meets West
paragraphs: Chinese (Cantonese) and Portuguese are official languages. The Historic Centre of Macau, with Portuguese churches, squares and Chinese temples such as the A-Ma Temple, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The ruins of St. Paul's Cathedral are its best-known landmark.

Macanese cuisine, a fusion of Portuguese, Chinese and other influences, is recognised by UNESCO; Portuguese egg tarts and African chicken are famous dishes. The Macau Grand Prix is a famous street racing event.

politics.heading: Special Administrative Region
paragraphs: Macau has its own legal system, currency and customs, while Beijing handles defence and foreign affairs. The Chief Executive is chosen by an election committee. Macau adopted national security laws earlier and with less opposition than Hong Kong, and pro-democracy candidates have been barred from elections.

economy.heading: World gambling capital
paragraphs: Macau is the world's largest gambling centre by revenue, and casinos provide most government revenue, giving it one of the world's highest GDPs per person. The economy depends heavily on visitors from mainland China.

The government is encouraging diversification into tourism, conventions, finance and traditional Chinese medicine, and closer integration with Hengqin island and the Greater Bay Area. The currency is the pataca.
